content.title: About
content.content: Bulgur is a pre‑cooked, dried and cracked wheat of hard varieties. In this version a plant fat is added, which raises its energy value and gives a richer taste. The product is commonly used in Middle Eastern dishes, salads, side dishes and vegetarian patties.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bulgur retains most of the nutrients of whole wheat, including fiber and B‑vitamins.
The added fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E and carotenoids.
Bulgur cooks quickly: just pour hot water over it and let it stand for 10–15 minutes.
In traditional Middle Eastern cuisine bulgur is often served as couscous or tabbouleh.
Dry bulgur can be stored for up to a year in a cool, dry place.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports normal digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs provide sustained energy, making bulgur a good choice for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Contains plant fats
items.content: Added plant fats supply essential fatty acids and aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bulgur is rich in thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides magnesium, iron and phosphorus, important for bones, muscles and blood formation.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy should avoid bulgur.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The added fat increases the product’s calories, so portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Bulgur contains small amounts of oxalates, which may be a concern for individuals prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fat‑added bulgur can be used in salads (tabbouleh), as a side dish for meat or fish, in vegetable casseroles, vegetarian patties and soups. Typically it is poured over with hot water or broth and left to absorb.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bulgur in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and light. For long‑term storage keep it in the refrigerator or freezer.
